chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub informed us, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad narrated to us from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, who said: Nasr ibn Muhammad ibn Qaboos narrated to me from Mansur ibn al-Sindi, from Abu Dawood al-Mustarraq, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Malik al-Juhani, from al-Harith ibn al-Mugheera, from al-Asbagh ibn Nabata, who said:

I came to the Commander of the Faithful, Ali, one day and found him pondering and scratching the ground. I said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, are you scratching the ground out of desire for it?' He said: 'No, by Allah. I have not desired it nor have I desired this worldly life for a moment. But my thought is on a child who will be born from my loins. He is the Mahdi, who will fill it with equity and justice, as it was filled with oppression and tyranny. There will be confusion and occultation for him. Some people will go astray in it and others will be guided.' I said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, how long will that confusion and occultation last?' He said: 'Years of time.' I said: 'Will that really happen?' He said: 'Yes! As it is created.' I said: 'Will I reach that time?' He said: 'How far is that from you, O Asbagh! Those are the best of this nation with the pious ones of this Progeny.' I said: 'Then what will happen after that?' He said: 'Allah will do what He wills, for He has wills, ends, and conclusions.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali (as) say about the Mahdi's occultation and justice?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam Ali (as) reveals his deep contemplation of the Mahdi, explicitly linking the future era of occultation (*ghayba*) and confusion (*hira*) to the purification of the faithful. The Imam’s response to Al-Asbagh’s question about witnessing the event underscores the distinction between the general populace and the 'chosen ones' of the Progeny, emphasizing that the ultimate outcome rests solely with Divine Will.
